lp.title: Wireframes that live in your own repo.
lp.lede: Pencil Viewer opens <link>.pen</link> files straight from GitHub, edits them in your browser, and commits them back. No account, no server, no storage bill.
lp.log.1: Add an empty state to the cart screen
lp.log.2: Even out spacing on the item rows
lp.proof.caption: On the left, a .pen file in a repository. On the right, the screen it draws. Edit it, commit it, and the change lands in the git history you already read.
lp.what.title: What it does
lp.what.repo.title: Reads and writes your repo
lp.what.repo.desc: Pick a branch, open a .pen, write a message, commit. Files move between GitHub and your browser and nowhere else.
lp.what.edit.title: A real editor
lp.what.edit.desc: Move, resize, align, undo. A layers panel, a command palette, and vim keys if you want them.
lp.what.render.title: Draws the whole format
lp.what.render.desc: Frames with flex layout, gradients, shadows, icon fonts, and $token variables resolved from the document.
lp.what.history.title: History you already trust
lp.what.history.desc: Every save is a commit. Open an older version, read it, and restore it.
lp.what.phone.title: Reads on a phone
lp.what.phone.desc: Editing panels fold away on small screens so the canvas fills them. Review a wireframe from anywhere.
lp.what.extras.title: Optional extras
lp.what.extras.desc: URL sharing, live collaboration, an MCP bridge for Claude Code, and an AI design review. All off unless you turn them on.
lp.cost.title: Why it stays free
lp.cost.body: Pencil Viewer stores nothing. The app is static files on GitHub Pages, and your designs sit in your own repository. There is no database to grow, so there is no bill to grow with it.
lp.try.title: Open a file
lp.try.note: Connect a repository, or just drop one file and look at it without signing in to anything.
lp.entry.desc: Your token stays in this browser's localStorage, and requests go straight to GitHub.
